theorem_title: Retained cover input survives a protected-memory update
formal_statement:
theorem ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockSourceCoverInput.Input.of_kept {μ ν : ℕ → ℤ} {h maps candidates histL histR bound : ℕ}
    (H : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockSourceCoverInput.Input μ h maps candidates histL histR) (K : _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.Light.Kept μ ν bound)
    (hmaps : maps+2*(464*h)*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalEncoding.scheduleSize h ≤ bound)
    (hcandidates : candidates+_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.GlobalEncoding.scheduleSize h ≤ bound)
    (hleft : histL+_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverSchedule.rows h*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LocalCoverBounds.localPrime h ≤ bound)
    (hright : histR+_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LightLocalCoverSchedule.rows h*_root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.LocalCoverBounds.localPrime h ≤ bound) :
    _root_.ThreeSum1960614.Machine.ThreeSum.BlockSourceCoverInput.Input ν h maps candidates histL histR := by sorry
natural_language_statement:
Suppose $\mu$ stores cover input for size $h$ at its coefficient, candidate, and two histogram bases. If $\nu$ agrees below bound $b$, and every array ends by $b$ using its specified schedule and local-prime length, then the identical cover-input predicate holds in $\nu$.

This transport permits source construction to reuse protected coefficient and histogram tables after intervening calls.
